propositions: Source code comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, and dated incident narratives that rot and become stale over time due to Gerrit rebase-on-submit and retention window expiry.

A detector scans for rot-prone patterns (SHA-like hex ≥7 chars, run/job/thread IDs ≥8 digits, date+incident-verb combinations) in code comments and docstrings, accepting only ticket/epic/bug/story IDs, word-triple aliases, or 'context: external' escape hatches.

Sixteen detector-hit sites across src/ and tests/ must be remediated by either citing a ticket-system ID, dropping rot-prone tokens while preserving current-state prose, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions locatable via git log.

A new CI guard (scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py) must be wired into the build workflow to block reintroduction of rot-prone comments, with zero in-tree suppressions and a self-exclusion mechanism for its own unit-test fixtures.

The acceptor must correctly reject false positives ('bug surfaced' phrasing and path names matching word-triple pattern) while accepting legitimate ticket IDs in 4x4 grouping and sentence-final word-triple alias forms.
Policy documentation must be added to CONTRIBUTING.md clarifying that source comments capture current state and rationale only, while historical incident detail belongs in the ticket system.
